2014_063_050614mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 6, 2014, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, combining recognitions, five sets of minutes, the March 2014 Treasurer's Report and check register, seven bid awards, and Oakland Schools' proposed FY 2014-15 budget. The central action item was appointment of a successor to retiring Superintendent Dr. Barbara Fowler, with finalists Dr. Richard Machesky and Dr. Steve Matthews following interviews on April 21 and April 29 and site visits on May 1. Under Section 624 of the Revised School Code the Board also resolved to express support for the Oakland ISD budget, which projects $287.8 million in revenue against $298.1 million in expenditures.

## Meeting
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, May 6, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

## Recognitions
Mary Curl, secretary at Morse Elementary, named Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year from nine nominees and 2014 county winner of the Betty Campion Award, presented by Dr. Vickie Markavitch of Oakland Schools. A State of Michigan Declaration of Special Tribute honored Dr. Barbara Fowler, retiring after 31 years. Thirty-six retirees were listed, each receiving a clock. A resolution marked National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 5-9, 2014.

## Consent agenda and minutes
Items A-H included minutes of the April 1 regular meeting, the April 21 and April 29 special board workshops, the April 22 special meeting and April 22 workshop, the March 2014 Treasurer's Report, Air Filters Bid 9775, and retirement of the superintendent. April 1 actions: 14-030 consent agenda; 14-031 ratifying the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA tentative agreement of March 22, 2014 covering April 1, 2014 through June 30, 2015; 14-032 personnel (new hire Francine Newman); 14-033 the 2013-14 budget amendment; 14-034 a First Student transportation contract for 2014/2015, 2015/2016 and 2016/2017 - all 7-0. On April 22, resolution 14-035 approved computer equipment purchases from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, 5-2 with Miletti and Schmidt opposed.

## Oakland ISD FY 2014-15 proposed budget (item 8.A/8.B)
Presented by Mark Rajter under Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624), which requires ISD submission by May 1 and a constituent-district resolution by June 1. Total revenue $287.8 million, including property tax revenue of $166.7 million; total expenditures $298.1 million, of which transfers to LEAs and other funds are $128.8 million. Property tax collection declined 24.5% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, a cumulative loss of $194.4 million; the FY 2008 base levy was $216.9 million. FY 2015 special education program support and subsidies total $112,844,000, including a PA-18 base distribution of $110,264,000. The Troy Board expressed support solely for the purpose of complying with Section 624.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education on May 6, 2014, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITIONS. Nine nominees were named for the 2013-2014 Outstanding Support Staff Award: Mary Curl (Secretary, Morse Elementary), Lois Hurdle (Secretary, TRC/Curriculum & Instruction), Krishna Patel (ESL Tutor, Smith Middle School), Becky Murphy (Secretary, Schroeder Elementary), Erin Prendergast (Para Educator, Troy Union Elementary), Sue Younan (ELL Parent Liaison, Costello/Wass/Troy Union), Fran Mahoney (Health Care Aide, Larson Middle School), Margaret Burchi (Title 1 Tutor, Larson Middle School) and Karen Guilbert (Health Care Aide, Costello Elementary). Mary Curl was named Employee of the Year and the 2014 county winner of the Betty Campion Outstanding Support Staff Award, presented by Dr. Vickie Markavitch, Superintendent of Oakland Schools. A State of Michigan Declaration of Special Tribute honored Superintendent Dr. Barbara Fowler, retiring after 31 years, read by President Nancy Philippart. Thirty-six retirees were listed with years of service, among them Mark Andrus (Technology Education, Larson MS, 40), Julianne Cover (Media Specialist, Barnard & Hamilton, 41), Mary Haezebrouck (Principal, Barnard, 38), Pam Mathers (Principal, Hamilton, 41), Mary McDermott (Health, Troy High, 41), Joseph Brandonisio (Biology, Troy High, 34 1/2) and Dr. Barbara Fowler (Superintendent, 31); Jasen Witt read names and President Philippart presented each a clock. A resolution recognized National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 5-9, 2014.

CONSENT AGENDA AND MINUTES. Items A-H covered minutes of the April 1, 2014 regular meeting, the April 21, 2014 special board workshop, the April 22, 2014 special meeting, the April 22, 2014 board workshop and the April 29, 2014 special board workshop, plus the March 2014 Treasurer's Report, Air Filters Bid 9775, and Retirement of the Superintendent. April 1 minutes (Troy High School, 7:03 p.m. to 10:12 p.m., about 200 in the audience; Philippart, Edmunds, Hauff, Fleming, Miletti, Schmidt, Underwood present; secretary Karl D. Schmidt) record 21 Outstanding Teacher Award nominees, three forwarded to Oakland Schools (Ann Lenihan, 2nd grade, Costello; Jennifer Taylor, math, Boulan Park MS; John Morrison, physics, Troy High), with Mrs. Lenihan named District Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year car lease donated by the Suburban Collection; 90 Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grants; and MSGCU cash grant awards announced by Tina Aleshker. Resolutions: 14-030 consent agenda, 7-0; 14-031 ratifying the tentative agreement of March 22, 2014 with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA for April 1, 2014 through June 30, 2015, 7-0; 14-032 personnel, new hire Francine Newman, an added FTE for speech services, 7-0; 14-033 amending the 2013-14 general appropriations - General Fund $133,770,738, Special Revenue Funds $8,325,771, Debt Service Funds $12,287,912, Capital Projects Funds none, Internal Service Fund $25,000 - 7-0; and 14-034 authorizing a First Student transportation contract for 2014/2015, 2015/2016 and 2016/2017, 7-0. Curriculum reports came from Kris Karbon (secondary math for grades 8-12, the Big Ideas Math high school series and Precalculus with Limits; high school health, Glencoe Health and Glencoe Human Sexuality approved by the Sex Education Advisory Board) and Anne Mull on Fall 2013 MEAP results for grades 3-9, with Troy's county ranks of 3rd in reading, 1st in math, 2nd in science, 2nd in writing and 5th in social studies. At the April 22, 2014 special meeting resolution 14-035 awarded computer equipment as a 2014 Capital Projects Fund expenditure - Apple, Inc. iPads and iPad minis $1,652,050.00; CDWG iPad cases $153,000.00; Sehi, Inc. Hewlett Packard laptops $58,680.00; total $1,863,730.00 - carried 5-2 with Miletti and Schmidt voting no. The same meeting adopted the Classrooms and Kids budget proposal resolution, 7-0, citing providing $250 to $291 per pupil by eliminating $186 million in certain categoricals. The April 29 special workshop held second public interviews of Dr. Steve Matthews, superintendent of Novi Community Schools, and Dr. Richard Machesky, assistant superintendent secondary instruction, with MASB representatives Rodney Green and Donna Oser attending the April 21 and April 29 sessions.

PERSONNEL AND CURRICULUM. Item 6.A reported the superintendent search assisted by the Michigan Association of School Boards, with first and second round public interviews on April 21 and April 29 and site visits to both candidates' districts on May 1; finalists were Dr. Richard Machesky and Dr. Steve Matthews. Item 6.B provided for the appointment resolution with a roll call roster of Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds, with contract approval to follow at a regular meeting. Items 7.A and 7.B adopted Glencoe Health 2013 edition and Glencoe Human Sexuality, and The Big Ideas Math Common Core High School Series with Precalculus with Limits by Ron Larson, for grades 9-12 in 2014-2015.

OAKLAND ISD BUDGET. Item 8.A presented the Oakland Schools FY 2014-2015 proposed budgets, noting that effective in 2004 Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624) requires each ISD to submit its budget to local districts no later than May 1 and each constituent board to adopt a supporting or disapproving resolution no later than June 1. Property tax forecasts show FY 2014-15 up 1.75%, FY 2015-16 up 2.75% and FY 2016-17 through FY 2018-19 up 3.50%, with a decline from the FY 2008 base of $(50.2)M in FY 2014-15; annual collections declined 24.5% from FY 2008 to FY 2014, a cumulative loss of $194.4 million and an estimated $244.6 million through FY15, against an FY 2008 base year levy of $216.9 million and an expected FY 2015 levy of $166.7 million. Assumptions include interest earnings of $300K for all funds combined compared with $7.7 million in FY07, stable state aid, no personal property tax loss in FY15, a QSCB interest subsidy reduced by 7.2%, a 1% pay increase subject to bargaining, a retirement rate of 25.62% adding $326,000 in cost under MPSERS retirement reform, and health insurance hard-cap employee contributions averaging 20% of premium. Total FY 2015 revenue of $287.8 million comprises property tax $166.7 (58%), other financing sources $7.8 (3%), new grant award funding $73.4 (25%), estimated grant carry-over $8.4 (3%), state revenue $8.1 (3%) and other local revenue $23.4 (8%). Total expenditures of $298.1 million comprise transfers to LEAs and other funds $128.8 (43.2%), grant related expenditures $81.8 (27.5%), personnel $56.7 (19.0%), purchased services, supplies and dues/fees $21.9 (7.4%), debt service $4.0 (1.3%), capital outlay and other $3.9 (1.3%) and utilities $1.0 (0.3%). The General Education Fund five-year forecast shows 2014-15 revenue $23.8 million and expenditures $24.1 million, an operating deficit of (.3), end-of-year fund balance $2.6 million and unreserved fund balance at 10.7% of expenditures, declining to $1.3 million and 5.3% by 2018-19. FY 2015 special education program support and subsidies total $112,844,000: PA-18 base distribution $110,264,000, Section 24 subsidy and other $220,000, group homes $1,910,000, Havenwick $150,000, and assistive technology equipment $300,000; the PA-18 base distribution increased $2.36M from FY14, and from FY13 to FY15 the increase equals the SEF revenue increase of $2.1M. Special education forecasts 2014-15 revenue $129.6 million and expenditures $129.5 million with total end-of-year fund balance $2.2 million and restricted fund balance at 5.00% net of LEA transfers. Career Focused Education forecasts 2014-15 revenue $32.4 million and expenditures $34.2 million, a deficit of (1.7), and restricted end-of-year fund balance $3.1 million at 9.1% of expenditures. Grants and funded projects total $81.8M ($73.4M new awards, $8.4M carry over), including a $5.5M MiCRSI grant under appeal by another applicant, $63.2M in direct transfers to districts and $18.6M in ISD-administered grants including JobLink at $5.7M. Item 8.B resolved that the Troy Board of Education received and reviewed the proposed budget and expressed its support, stating that support is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624, with a copy to be forwarded to the Oakland Schools Board of Education no later than June 1, 2014; the certification cites the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267.

POLICIES. Second readings and adoption followed first readings on April 1, 2014. Board Policy C-1402, Smoking, was revised to Tobacco-Free Schools, prohibiting use or sale of tobacco products and non-tobacco nicotine products, including e-cigarettes, shisha or hookah, snus and dissolvable products, by any person, at any time (24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year), in any location and at any event, excluding physician-prescribed nicotine replacement therapy; adopted February 2, 1999, revised September 2003, April 20, 2010 and February 12, 2014. Board Policy G-1005, Nondiscrimination, cites Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, and adds sexual orientation, gender identity, socioeconomic status, perceived religion and association with a protected person to the protected class list, naming the Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources as coordinator at 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098-4799; adopted July 10, 2007, revised February 12, 2014. Board Policy J-2012, Anti-Bullying, defines prohibited conduct, bars retaliation and false accusation, requires prompt reporting to the building principal, investigation, parent notification, annual reports of verified incidents to the school board, designates the superintendent as Responsible School Official, and adopts definitions of telecommunications access device and service provider from Section 219a of the Michigan Penal Code, 1931 PA 328, MCL 750.219a; adopted June 5, 2012, revised March 6, 2014.
